liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews, 2 other sources): Ranks The Other One among the finest the reviewer has heard, at least top three; Names The Other One as a gem of the show [2][6][28][32]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (3 reviews): Singles out the Scarlet into Fire segment, with Phil's bass playing described as especially powerful; Calls the Scarlet-Fire possibly one of the best ever, and the second set a party favorite [24][26][30]
- **Lazy Lightnin'** (2 reviews): Remembers the first-set Lazy Lightning as outstanding; Calls the Lazy Lightning into Supplication pairing a Bob highlight [27][32]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Notes the first set with Candyman, Tennessee Jed and Peggy-O would please Jerry fans [32]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 other source): Notes a noodle section leading into Truckin' is included on the recording [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-04-23.143127.fob.senn421.wise.clugston.miller.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 182 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1983-04-23.143126.fob.senn421.wise.clugston.miller.flac1648**: audience recording; 25 songs; 182 min [2]
- **gd1983-04-23.163834.senn441.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 188 min [6]
- **gd1983-04-23.fob.senn421.coyotte.muletaper.88482.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 180 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [12]
- **gd83-04-23.set2-sbd.miller.29469.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 114 min; rated 4/5 by 16 [20]. Said about its sound: This soundboard covers only the second set; the reviewer wishes the first set were included; Soundboard sounds sweet but is incomplete, lacking the first set; Soundboard is accurate but lacks deep audience bass, has channel wobble, and Scarlet-Fire sounds fast-pitched [25][27][28]

## Around the show

- Attended both nights; says the building shook, and describes New Haven as a shady city [27]
- A door pop let in hundreds of fans without tickets; the band opened with a song about not having sense to run [29]
- Describes the venue as a grimy little arena with a crazy escalator; reviewer's car was broken into the next year [30]
- Attendee says Phil was turned up loud from the start, though everyone played well [31]
- Says the venue was imploded two years earlier and links a video of it [34]
- Says Phil dropped plenty of bass bombs throughout April 1983 [24]
- Calls this the best Scarlet-Fire the reviewer has on tape, compared with an audience CDR [28]
- Considers it one of the most underrated shows of the 1983 tour [31]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-04-23.143127.fob.senn421.wise.clugston.miller.flac2496**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jim Wise's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell UDXLII C90) [1]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to make the recording complete [1]
- **gd1983-04-23.143126.fob.senn421.wise.clugston.miller.flac1648**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller and Jim Wise; source: Jim Wise's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell UDXLII C90) [2]
- **gd1983-04-23.163834.senn441.eaton.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Rob Eaton; transferred by Rob Eaton, Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Rob Eaton's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics (16th row, DFC) > Sony D5M [6]. Also: Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 source supplies a 4:09 Drums patch, plus Not Fade Away and the encores [6]
- **gd1983-04-23.fob.senn421.coyotte.muletaper.88482.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Rick "Coyotte" Colyard; transferred by Muletaper; source: 2-Sennheiser MD421's (location: FOB-11th row DFC @6 ft high on stand) > Sony D5 (Two maxell UD-XL2-cassettes) [12]. Also: Reviewer had a cassette copy of this same mix, worn out from heavy play [31]
- **gd83-04-23.set2-sbd.miller.29469.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: flac16 SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Dat -> CD [20]
